source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Acknowledge the message silently because verbal confirmation is unnecessary when both clinicians are in the same room.","B":"Repeat the message back and obtain confirmation from the original sender that the information was understood correctly.","C":"Ask a third team member what the sender probably meant instead of confirming the information with the original sender.","D":"Write the message down for later review because documentation alone closes the communication loop during the exchange."}}
source_row.rationale: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS defines check-back as closed-loop communication: the receiver repeats information and the original sender confirms or corrects it. Option B is correct. Option A omits feedback, Option C substitutes a third party for the source, and Option D mistakes later documentation for real-time closed-loop confirmation.
source_row.source_detail: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS — Check-Back (Repeat-Back): a closed-loop communication strategy in which the sender initiates a message, the receiver accepts and repeats it back, and the sender verifies/corrects the information to confirm shared understanding. Current AHRQ TeamSTEPPS communication tool; page last reviewed 2023-07 and live federal resource rechecked 2026-08-15. Blueprint corrected to Management of Care because the tested competency is interprofessional communication/care coordination. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: continuity/transfer of care, collaboration, legal/regulatory scope, quality improvement, leadership and professional-practice activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: During a team huddle, one clinician gives another clinician important information. Which response best demonstrates AHRQ check-back communication?
